plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like, showy flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a classic winter bloomer in gardens, with thousands of cultivars in single, semi-double, and fully double forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, peaking in January through March
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant used to make all true teas, and Camellia japonica has been cultivated in Japan for over a thousand years.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub that produces spidery, ribbon-like, strongly fragrant flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter. The petals curl up in freezing temperatures to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms.
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can tolerate freezing temperatures by curling their petals, and extracts from the genus are used in traditional astringent skin products.

plants.name: Jasminum nudiflorum
plants.description: A sprawling deciduous shrub with arching green stems that bear bright yellow flowers before the leaves emerge. It brings cheerful color to cold gardens, walls, and banks during winter thaws.
plants.location: Native to northern China; naturalized or cultivated in the UK, Europe, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Unlike many jasmines, winter jasmine has no fragrance, but it is valued for blooming when almost nothing else in the garden does.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall stems topped with round umbels of trumpet-shaped blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, it creates dramatic displays along roadsides, borders, and coastal gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December to February
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely grown in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California, and naturalized in some regions
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily; its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
